findings.reason: §2 must reconcile its topic-as-unit rule with the pre-existing per-node subtree allocation and §3 must write the rule into the prompt that already carries a conflicting figure path, or neither section states what dispatch will actually enforce.
findings.text: the plan's topic-directory allocation rule never cites the figure-specific allocation machinery that already exists in dispatch: `_landing_fragment_paths` allocates every node its own `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/` subtree (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2032-2034), granted into the node's write scope by `_grant_landing_write_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2044-2083), and `_shared_landing_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1955-2003) already names `docs/figures/<plan>` as the plan-wide figure topic; the same missed census continues at reckon/crew/prompts.py:167 (the plan-node landing contract tells the worker to write figures under its own `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/`) and reckon/crew/prompts.py:204 (the brief contract says `docs/figures/<topic>/`) — three existing figure-path surfaces — so §1's claim that existing guidance covers "only where to put them" under `docs/figures/<topic>/` is understated and §3's list of the two surfaces a worker reads omits the dispatch prompt a worker actually reads

findings.reason: §2 asserts a rule that the mechanism it names as "already half-implementing" it actively negates at the plan-wide topic, so the section must either extend `_shared_landing_paths` (remove the plan figure topic from the shared set) or restate its unit as the per-node subtree the code enforces.
findings.text: §2 states the figure topic directory is claimed by exactly one node and a second declarer is refused, but the existing owner of figure-topic treatment, `_shared_landing_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1955-2003), already defines the plan-wide figure topic `docs/figures/<plan>` as a "shared landing path" every node holds, and `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` exempts any peer claim whose absolute path is in that shared set (`if claim.absolute_path.resolve() in shared: continue`, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2705), so a second node declaring the plan's own figure topic is admitted rather than refused — the guard §2 rests on does not fire for the plan-level topic, which is the ordinary case for a plan's own figures

findings.reason: a section that adds a refusal family must name the retirement or the impossibility in its own text, and the section's stated rule would otherwise be silently inert against the current sibling-admitting guard, which the open decision's own "yes-if-filenames-are-disjoint" branch confirms is the live behaviour.
findings.text: §2 adds a refusal family: "the claim covers the tree" refuses a second node writing a disjoint filename inside a claimed topic, which the current dispatch admits (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2707-2710 admits disjoint sibling leaves under a common prefix), and §2 asserts this while leaving the sibling-writers decision open, recording no interface surface retired or merged (no public definition, CLI option or MCP view is named as replaced) and no reason nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design adds no module; it is a stated rule, a pinning test set and a mechanism comment, so there is no interface smaller than the behaviour it hides to judge for depth.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 declares the figure topic an exclusive claim, but the mechanism that owns figure-topic treatment, `_shared_landing_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1955), already assigns the plan-wide figure topic non-exclusive shared-landing semantics and exempts it from the very refusal §2 relies on (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2705).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2's exclusivity rule adds a refusal family (refusing a disjoint filename under a claimed topic) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1/§2 propose the topic directory as the figure allocation unit and characterise existing guidance as covering only "where to put them", but a figure-specific allocation owner already exists and is nowhere named (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2034), and a second figure-path surface the plan's census omits (reckon/crew/prompts.py:167).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; the rule attaches to the existing dispatch claim check rather than a parallel mechanism, which is the honest form.
